newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Fernz sees strong second half profit.
newsitem.headline: Fernz sees strong second half profit.

text.p: Chemicals company Fernz Corp Ltd on Wednesday said the general outlook for demand in the second half was good.
It said approximately two thirds of the annual budgeted profit was forecast to be generated in the second half and cash flow from operating activities would be strong.
At its annual meeting last October, Fernz forecast an annual profit of NZ$47.3 million.
Fernz reported an unaudited tax paid profit of NZ$16.1 million for the 6 months to November 30, 1996, up 3.4 percent on the previous comparable period.
Earnings before interest and taxation increased by 30.5 percent in the period.

Depreciation and amortisation amounted to NZ$14.4 million (last year $12.5 million), interest was $13.2 million (last year $7.6 million) and taxation had been provided for at $5.8 million (last year $3.8 million).
Fernz said 30 percent of the $380.8 million turnover for the six months was generated in New Zealand, 51 percent in Australia and 19 percent in other markets.
The results include five months trading of the Laporte Group Australia and Akzo Nobel Crop Protection business in The Netherlands, both consolidated for the first time, Fernz said.
In addition, Fidene Consolidated and the impact of acquisition of the balance of the shareholding in Pacific Raw Materials had been included in the group result.

"In general the outlook for demand for our products in the second half is good. Approximately two thirds of the annual budgeted profit is forecast to be generated in the second half and cash flow from operating activities will be strong," Fernz said.
"The development initiatives and projects currently in place should begin to create shareholder value in the second half of the 1997 financial year.
"The medium and long term outlook for the company is positive and the directors consider that growth prospects and value creation opportunities are good."
